summary:
Hand Me the Earth is an interactive, gesture-controlled platform that makes NASA satellite radar data more accessible, engaging, and easier to understand.

Taking on the challenge of Dancing With The SARs, our project transforms complex Earth observation data into an immersive experience. Users can navigate a 3D globe using hand gestures, select locations, and explore satellite imagery across different points in time to visualize changes in Earth's surface.

In addition to simplifying scientific data, our project addresses accessibility barriers with traditional digital interfaces. By offering touch-free hand gestures alongside mouse controls, we aim to create a more inclusive experience for older adults, people with disabilities, students, and curious learners.

Hand Me the Earth bridges the gap between complex satellite technology and everyday users, encouraging environmental awareness while demonstrating how interactive technology can make Earth science more approachable. We believe understanding our changing planet should be an opportunity available to everyone.
details:
Hand Me the Earth is an interactive, gesture-controlled platform that makes NASA satellite radar data easier to explore and understand. Users can navigate a 3D globe, explore environmental events such as floods, earthquakes, and deforestation, and compare satellite observations over time.

We built the application using JavaScript, React, Three.js, MediaPipe, Python, and Cloudflare, integrating NASA NISAR data with real-time hand tracking and interactive visualizations.

Our innovation combines Earth science with intuitive, hands-on exploration. By offering gesture-based navigation alongside traditional controls, we aim to reduce accessibility barriers for older adults and people with disabilities.

Throughout development, we prioritized accessibility, scientific accuracy, usability, and educational value. Our goal is to make Earth's environmental changes more understandable and engaging for everyone.
